LESSON: NUTRITION

Grade: SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: BIOLOGY
Strand: Anatomy and Physiology of Animals
Topic 3.1: Nutrition
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Nutrition, part of Anatomy and Physiology of Animals in SNE  /  visual-impairment / Grade 10 BIOLOGY.

Key inquiry question: How do insects and birds feed?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Nutrition together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: The learner cooperates with others while collecting fresh specimens of insects to

observe their mouthparts.

● Digital literacy: The learner uses digital devices to access and watch animations/videos on mouth parts of different

insects and beaks of birds.

● Citizenship: Learners demonstrate tolerance, express themselves as they understand different viewpoints as they

participate in environmental conservation in the community.

Values:
● Responsibility: The learner diligently observes safety precautions as they collect fresh specimens of insects to observe

their mouthparts.

39

● Social justice: The learner promotes equity, equality and gender consideration in distribution of learning resources as

well as assigning responsibilities during group activities.

● Respect: The learners show high regard for each other as they work in small groups to observe different birds and

their feeding habits.

● Integrity: The learners are committed to duty as they participate in environmental conservation and report their

findings on the feeding habits of birds.

Suggested Learning Resources

● Fresh specimens of locust/grasshopper/cockroach

● Realia, images, animations

● Photographs/photomicrographs, charts

● Tactile/ mounted beaks of different birds

● Protective equipment (gloves)

● Digital devices with assistive technology such as screen readers, talkback, refreshable braille display, screen

magnifiers

● Reference materials in print with appropriate font size and colour contrast

● Braille reference materials

Key Skills:

● Relate the structure of mouthparts of insects to their functions,

● Relate the structure of beaks of birds to their functions.
